metadata.rebase.open_question:
Clean linear rebase (ac6fed3 -> e6de0ac on base e72252e), but the merged head is RED on a BASE-owned pin. Rebase-induced only: base alone GREEN and the contributor's own pre-rebase head GREEN; only the composition fails. NOT repaired here -- this is a genuine contract collision, and picking a winner rewrites either a pinned base contract or the PR's headline mechanism. Review lane decides.
(1) COLLISION: base 5bffaf7 (PR #282) added test_work_bead_resolution_discriminator_is_pinned, a ROLE-SPECIFIC rule -- the refinery rotates wisps in-session, so it must resolve every wisp from the bare ${GC_BEAD_ID:-} plus the live assignee query, NEVER a spawn trigger (the deacon is exempted as a singleton that exits each turn). That test did not exist at the contributor's branch point. PR #379 replaces all refinery sites with gc's own documented idiom ${GC_BEAD_ID:-${GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID:-$(gc hook current --id-only)}} -- printed verbatim by `gc hook current --help`. Failure is the COUNT pin: "every refinery wisp resolution must be the bare form (1 of 7)". #282's NAME pin greps GC_TRIGGER_WORK_BEAD_ID while #379 uses GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID, so the name pin never fires -- the review lane may need to widen it either way.
(2) EVIDENCE that #282's staleness concern is live, not theoretical: in this live pool session GC_BEAD_ID is EMPTY while GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID is SET, so arm 2 decides and arm 3 (gc hook current --id-only) is UNREACHABLE in normal operation. That contradicts the premise in `gc hook current --help` ("a pool session's shell never receives $GC_BEAD_ID or $GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID"). CAVEAT, stated honestly: this session claimed once and never rotated, so divergence was NOT observed -- the hazard is specifically post-rotation, when the spawn trigger still names the burned wisp. Note the PR's own new test runs `env -u GC_BEAD_ID -u GC_TRIGGER_BEAD_ID`, so it never exercises the trigger arm at all.
(3) SEPARATE mechanical incompleteness: base e72252e (PR #288) added a 6th CURRENT_WISP site (mol-refinery-patrol.toml line 283, invalid-target-branch escalation) that the contributor never saw. Merged head is internally inconsistent: 6 sites converted, 1 still bare. Deliberately NOT converted -- it does not clear the red (7-of-7 non-bare is still red on the count pin) and would extend the contested mechanism on no authority. Whichever way the collision is resolved, this site must move with the others.
VERIFIED GREEN: the PR's own two new tests PASS on the merged head when run in isolation (base's earlier fail() exits the suite before they are reached, so their result was shadowed). tests/test_gascity_pack_inference_gate.py 87 passed; formula TOML parses. Adoption exactness: base->HEAD numstat == contributor's own MB->original-head exactly (3 files, +100/-32, matching GitHub); 2/3 files patch-id IDENTICAL, the test file differs by context shift only (added-line list byte-identical, 0 deletions both ways); 17 test defs <-> 17 invocations, bash -n clean; contributor authorship preserved. metadata.rebase.open_question: PR 298's two new bound tests are VACUOUS on the merged head and the bound is dead in production. (1) Vacuity: base's new single-flight lock gates the gc queries behind mkdir "$lock", and mkdir/rmdir are absent from STATUS_LINE_PROBE_TOOLS, so the restricted-PATH probes take the serve-stale branch and gc is never invoked. Control: reducing run_bounded to a bare passthrough leaves the whole suite GREEN. Adding mkdir+rmdir to the probe list makes it RED (FAIL: hanging query was never bounded where timeout(1) is absent). (2) The underlying defect is PRE-EXISTING, not rebase-induced: the same failure reproduces on the contributor's own unmodified head 51072bf in a scratch worktree, where no lock exists. Root cause is dash: kill rejects the -- separator, tty-less set -m turns job control off so no process group is created, and the unconditional wait then blocks for the child's full life. End-to-end under /bin/sh (dash): merged head did NOT bound a 25s hanging query (>40s), base bounds it at 4s -- so this head is WEAKER than base, which timeout 2s did bound. (3) Satisfiable: a green control (setsid for the child, drop the -- dash rejects, sweep before wait, with probes restored) passes both tests -- that is the fix direction, though setsid is util-linux and absent on macOS, so portability is a design call. Scope: repairing the conflict is this gate's job; rewriting the PR's headline mechanism is the review lane's.

metadata.rebase.open_question: BLOCKER for review lane, pre-existing in the PR and NOT rebase-induced: the process-group bound never fires under dash (/bin/sh on Debian/Ubuntu). Two causes: dash builtin kill rejects the -- separator (kill: Illegal number: -), and tty-less set -m fails ("can not access tty; job control turned off") so the child stays in the script own pgid and never becomes a group leader. Both kills no-op, then the unconditional wait $_rb_pid blocks for the child full lifetime - measured 25s+ against a 1s bound. Both new tests fail on the merged head AND on the contributor own pre-rebase head 51072bf; base lock had merely masked them. Note this makes the merged head WEAKER than base on Linux, where base timeout 2s did bound. Green control (setsid + drop --) passes both tests, so the tests are honest and satisfiable; but setsid is util-linux and absent on macOS, so the portable fix is a design call for review, not for this gate.
